gurkha--ghost.description: Introduced in 2012 and made with Abe Flores at PDR Cigars, Ghost wraps a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler in a dark Brazilian Arapiraca maduro leaf. It smokes medium to full, with white and black pepper over mocha, espresso and earth, and a sharp edge that gives it bite.

gurkha--evil.description: Evil is handmade in Nicaragua from a thick Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper, a Dominican binder and Nicaraguan long filler. Reviewers describe a dense, full-bodied smoke of wood, earth and pepper that turns towards cinnamon, leather and a late sweetness, with a long finish.

thirds.notes: Dry wood and earth over a peppery base, with hints of cinnamon and leather.
Leathery cinnamon spice and more wood, with a touch of sweetness and an occasional nutty note.
Sweet spice and leather intensify as the body reaches full; sweetness grows and the finish runs long.

sources.title: Scott's World of Cigars – Gurkha Evil Robusto
Some of the Finer Things – Gurkha Evil review

gurkha--125th-anniversary.description: Named for 1887, when Gurkha as a cigar name first appeared, this blend from the Pinar del Río factory in the Dominican Republic pairs a Brazilian Habano wrapper with an Ecuadorian binder and filler from Nicaragua, Brazil and the Dominican Republic. It opens sweet and spicy, then settles into creamy leather and earth.

thirds.notes: Sweet tobacco and earth with cedar, a hint of cinnamon, light black pepper and cocoa; the smoke feels full early on.
Leather and earth come forward, spice fades, and a creamy, nutty tone appears with a little wood.
Plain tobacco and cream dominate as the strength edges up to medium-full.

sources.title: Famous Smoke Cigar Advisor – Gurkha 125th Anniversary review
Cigar Obsession – Gurkha 125th Anniversary Rothchild review

gurkha--treinta.description: Released in 2019 to mark thirty years since Kaizad Hansotia bought the Gurkha name, Treinta is rolled at Aganorsa's TABSA factory from an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper, a Corojo 99 binder and Criollo 98 and Corojo 99 filler from Estelí and Jalapa. It is medium-bodied but full of flavour, moving from hay and leather to cocoa and coffee.

thirds.notes: Dry hay and leather with cedar-like wood, a little coffee and sharper pepper through the nose.
Sweeter and creamier, with leather, baking spice and a cocoa note that shows most on the retrohale.
Deeper and darker: coffee, soil, cocoa, leather and wood, with the strength rising.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Gurkha Treinta Toro

gurkha--heritage.description: Heritage is rolled in Nicaragua under an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper, with a Nicaraguan binder and filler drawn from Nicaragua, the Dominican Republic and the United States. Reviewers find leathery earth, spiced cedar and a mineral touch, with espresso and chocolate in the background and a smooth, oily texture.
